verdicts.quote: a Lightning app named "Grok Bot" containing one tab "Grok Bot" that renders the chat component ... Out of scope bounded here: Salesforce mobile app, Experience Cloud/guest, Utility-bar/Lightning Home placement

the bot reads and writes no standard or custom records (A-3), so no object or field permission is granted. It reads its own custom-metadata configuration only.

a permission set (name provisional, AD-5) grants the Grok Bot app and tab visibility, access to the Apex class(es) the component calls, and the External Credential principal. Only users it is assigned to can use the bot
verdicts.missing: Which permission or role is required to administer the bot (edit the config record, enter/rotate the key); spec only says "admins".

verdicts.quote: Transcript + history + pending flag | LWC memory of one tab | That user only; never sent to another client ... stored nowhere in Salesforce (A-4)
Each turn is one synchronous Apex transaction with exactly one callout and zero DML ... no pending DML before the callout
verdicts.missing: The spec states the DML-before-callout constraint but chooses a synchronous imperative call, not an asynchronous (Queueable/future/batch) design.

verdicts.quote: the key is stored in an External Credential (named principal) and used through a Named Credential ... The key never appears in source control, Apex, LWC, custom metadata, records, debug logs, error messages

verdicts.missing: CPU time limit is not named; heap value is marked unverified.

verdicts.quote: Apex tests use an `HttpCalloutMock` (no real network) and cover R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8 and R-10
Named Credential for `https://api.x.ai` ... Apex addresses the endpoint with the `callout:` form only.
imperative Apex call (one transaction) ... Apex returns a structured outcome → component appends the reply ... synchronous per turn ... No background jobs, no polling.
verdicts.missing: No asynchronous notification mechanism (platform event, polled status, LMS); the design relies on the call returning inline.

verdicts.quote: Idempotency: no idempotency key is sent; duplicate calls are possible after TIMEOUT ... A result appears only for the request that is still current.
verdicts.missing: No deduplication on the request/message; duplicates are acknowledged rather than prevented.
